text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a software development practice where team members frequently merge their code changes into a shared repository. To manage this, teams use CI pipelines, which are automated processes that run every time new code is pushed. First, the pipeline automatically builds the software to check if all parts compile correctly. Then, it runs a full suite of tests, including unit and integration tests. This approach is vital because it catches issues early, often within minutes of a change. By identifying bugs immediately, developers can fix them quickly, avoiding the nightmare of integrating for days at the end of a project. In short, CI keeps the software stable and development moving forward smoothly.
